releases.body:
Stable native accelerometer release after PR #58, “Supersample whole accelerometer glyphs,” merged as `bf44102c1cec8b27498fc98410a418be8e2a66c8`.

Release source is the exact physical-phone-tested PR head `340381176f8f7c89427bd1e41286a1e0ae1cf0d1`. The attached APK is the retained output from successful Actions run `35690545955`, artifact `10677804951`; it was not rebuilt for publication.

Physical MIRO A1 evidence for this exact APK:
- installed and launched successfully on the real ARMv7 phone;
- percentage-based vertical layout from PR #57 remains visually accepted;
- full-glyph 4×4 grayscale supersampling substantially improves X and other diagonal strokes;
- the resulting display was accepted for release, with a few glyphs still somewhat bubbly.

Known measurement issue:
- one observed stationary frame showed approximately X +1.2, Y +7.8, Z +0.1 m/s², whose Euclidean magnitude is about 7.9 m/s² rather than approximately 9.8 m/s²;
- this release therefore does not claim calibrated acceleration magnitude. The under-reading remains a separate measurement-path issue.

Provenance:
- PR #58: Supersample whole accelerometer glyphs
- PR head: `340381176f8f7c89427bd1e41286a1e0ae1cf0d1`
- merge commit: `bf44102c1cec8b27498fc98410a418be8e2a66c8`
- Actions run: `35690545955`
- retained artifact: `10677804951`
- APK SHA-256: `61885896fb66ec14b8325b2559ce3d784996dd9cbf74fe418e924eb48fd8632b`
- native package includes ARMv7, AArch64, and x86_64 libraries and no `classes.dex`.


## Recorded sensor replay

[![Recorded accelerometer replay](https://github.com/Ashtray-Archer/utilities-android-phone-user/releases/download/accelerometer-native-v0.2.0/accelerometer-native-v0.2.0-replay.gif)](https://github.com/Ashtray-Archer/utilities-android-phone-user/releases/download/accelerometer-native-v0.2.0/accelerometer-native-v0.2.0-replay.mp4)

[Watch the MP4 replay](https://github.com/Ashtray-Archer/utilities-android-phone-user/releases/download/accelerometer-native-v0.2.0/accelerometer-native-v0.2.0-replay.mp4)

This is a visualization reconstructed from a recorded retained-Float16 X/Y/Z sample sequence, not a screen recording.

Physical-device evidence actually observed:
- the APK installed and launched as the Accelerometer application;
- live X/Y/Z values and axis bars were visible;
- one captured frame showed `X -0.325 m/s²`, `Y +2.936 m/s²`, `Z +9.224 m/s²`;
- while the phone was rotated, the displayed values redrew continuously and the gravity component moved between device axes.

This is not a calibrated sensor test and is not evidence that Idriç generated the current C/NDK application core.

# Programmer's Unicode Picker 0.3.0 prerelease

This is the standalone Unicode-pad-style picker, not the Android keyboard/IME.

Open the app, tap characters into its text buffer, tap **COPY**, then paste into the target app. It does not ask to enable or select a keyboard and does not alter the system keyboard configuration.

## Included pages

- Unicode
- Math
- Punctuation
- Programming
- Regular Expressions
- Concept Separation
- Incantation Assistance
- Several Pastebins

The picker includes the current heavy programming assignment arrow `⟵`, while ordinary `←` remains available on the Unicode and Math pages.

## Android/runtime boundary

- native C APK using Android's platform `NativeActivity`
- no app Java or Kotlin
- no `classes.dex`
- no requested Android permissions
- arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, and x86_64 native libraries
- versionName 0.3.0 / versionCode 3

The Idriç source defines the picker pages and allowed key actions and generates the checked-in C layout snapshot; the mutable editing state and Android boundary remain C in this release.

## Verification

The release workflow checks the Idriç layout contract, runs the host C behavior/touch tests, builds and inspects the APK, and exercises the picker in an Android emulator before publishing the release.

The attached APK is debug-signed for sideload testing. It is not a Google Play production-signed artifact.

Scrolling revision: swipes that begin on tappable pictures now remain scroll gestures, large up/down controls make long choice lists easier to navigate, and the wings are larger with stronger color and outlines. Existing back, exit, picture-tap, and salon state behavior remains intact.

Touch/navigation revision: tapping the pictures performs the same actions as tapping their labels, interior screens have a large star back control, and every screen has a clear exit control. The graphical salon content from v0.2.1 remains intact.

Checked graphical salon preview: all four waiting-room animals render, zebra/horse/both unicorns remain visible throughout the salon, dresses cover the body, outfit/hair/makeup/accessory choices use pictures, the full snack-and-drink menu is illustrated, and the photo room is visual. Text-only state remains available only behind the disabled DEBUG_UI flag.

Graphical salon preview: the waiting room now shows all four animals, zebra/horse/both unicorns render throughout the salon, dresses cover the character body, outfit/hair/makeup/accessory choices have pictures, the snack-and-drink shop has illustrated items, and the photo room is visual. Text-only state is retained only behind the disabled DEBUG_UI flag.

First playable Godot salon preview. Choose the zebra, watch it blink, tap Dress up, and switch between two explicitly temporary prototype outfits. Zebra unicorn costume, wings, horn controls, snacks/drinks, and photo flow remain available.

Phone-approved canonical smooth-orbit explorer built from e0c5e779268eedea341f56ede07c1d1559e9d864.

Twenty-four remote pole singularities stay outside the visible region and follow independent smooth clockwise or counterclockwise circuits with gentle radial bending and slight ellipticity. The holomorphic field continues to evolve independently, preserving the approved whole-field motion while removing Brownian steering from the outer wanderers.

The APK was rebuilt and signature-verified from the merged main commit.

Corrected Android test APK from commit db36e2d5fa936019a3239de4fcb190b4b324611e.

The launcher opens directly into the live native EGL/OpenGL ES convergence explorer with editable zero and infinity controls. Both guided movies are packaged as Android-compatible H.264 Constrained Baseline, and CI played and captured each movie, rendered the explorer, and accepted an explorer touch on this exact APK before publication.

It uses the same repository test-only signing key as earlier GitHub APKs, so it installs as an update. It is not the separately signed Google Play production build.
This prerelease is tied to an older pre-rebase commit. Use v0.2.1, which is gated on guided-content playback and a live explorer touch.
This build has a known blank-movie playback problem on some Android devices. Use v0.2.1 instead.

Color-corrected public sideload build of the analytic-continuation lasso experiment from lasso commit f2e428e5807ddf39b284a79177346d02e4247f37.

Restores the original CIELUV/HCL domain-coloring palette while retaining the cheaper Blaschke phase/modulus accumulation. Package: org.isomorphisms.analyticcontinuation.lasso.dev. Android version code: 2.

This APK uses the same permanent non-production sideload signing key as Lasso Dev v0.1.0, so it updates that installation in place.
